- **Windows build:** <!-- output of: [Environment]::OSVersion.Version -->
- **Vendor / model / Lenovo MT:** <!-- e.g. Lenovo 21L1 -->
- **Partition style:** <!-- GPT or MBR -->
- **Intervening partition (v48+):** <!-- If the OS disk has a non-recovery partition between C: and the type-coded recovery partition, describe it: drive letter, size, filesystem, type code, BitLocker state. v48 handles exactly one intervening partition when it validates as an anchor; a `C: | D: | E: | Recovery` layout still defers. Skip if C: and the recovery partition are adjacent. -->
- **Windows Setup state:** <!-- output of: (Get-ItemProperty "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Setup\State" -Name ImageState -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ImageState -->
  <!-- IMAGE_STATE_COMPLETE, another value, or blank. Another value means the machine is in Audit Mode, OOBE, or a sysprep phase. -->
- **BitLocker state on C:** <!-- paste both fields from: manage-bde -status C: -->
  - **Protection Status:** <!-- Protection On / Protection Off -->
  - **Conversion Status:** <!-- Fully Decrypted / Fully Encrypted / Encryption In Progress / Decryption In Progress / Encryption Paused / Decryption Paused -->
  <!-- C:'s state matters only on the OS-fallback route. On the enable-only and dedicated-partition routes, production targets the recovery partition directly and does not depend on C:'s state. -->
- **Free space on the resize target:** <!-- current free, in GiB, and total size of the resize target in GiB -->
  <!-- Required if the run exited with a pre-shrink deferral (log line contains "Dedicated replacement deferred before partition deletion"). The free-space check refuses to shrink the resize target below a 3 GiB reserve, and the deferral reason names the projected post-shrink free space. The resize target is C: on the ordinary path, or the intervening anchor partition (typically D:) on the v48 `C: | D: | Recovery` path. The deferral reason in the log names which: "OS partition (C:)" or "anchor partition (disk X part Y)". Report the free space and total size of the target the deferral reason names. -->
- **Target recovery partition state:** <!-- run: .\scripts\Test-WinRE.ps1 and choose Option 1. Copy the "Target recovery partition state" block. -->
  <!-- This is the partition reagentc is registered to. It is what production prepares via Set-RecoveryPartitionReadyForWinRE. If the block says "BitLocker-managed", production will run manage-bde -off against it before calling reagentc /enable. -->
- **VMD hardware present:** <!-- output of the harness Option 1 "VMD hardware presence" block, or "yes/no" from BIOS if the harness cannot be run. VMD presence is one of the DesiredStateId inputs. -->
  <!-- If the harness reports "INDETERMINATE", copy the enumeration error line printed under it (the harness emits `PnP enumeration error: …` in the line below the INDETERMINATE verdict). The specific error text distinguishes a service issue from an antivirus/EDR block from a device in an error state. -->
- **Storage controllers present (v28+ harness):** <!-- output of the harness Option 1 "Storage controllers" block, if shown. The v49 pre-deployment storage-applicability gate compares the candidate image's INFs against these controllers. If the run deferred at the applicability gate, this block is what the maintainer needs. -->
- **State file fields:** <!-- if C:\Recovery\OEM\winre_state.json exists, paste: DesiredStateId, LastUpdated, LastEnableResult, and EnableFailureAttempts -->
  <!-- LastEnableResult and EnableFailureAttempts are optional in the JSON and default to "ok" / 0 if absent. LastUpdated distinguishes a run that reached the state-write point (timestamp newer than run start) from a deferral (timestamp unchanged). DesiredStateId is required for the maintainer to check whether the state file would be accepted on this machine. -->
  <!-- If you can run the harness, Option S "State file parity check" reports whether the on-disk state file matches the ID production would compute right now. As of v48 it also reports the stored and computed `LocalInputsId` so an offline-fallback mismatch can be diagnosed without running production. -->
- **Checkpoint file (if present):** <!-- copy `C:\ProgramData\OEM\Logs\winre_checkpoint.txt` verbatim. It carries the staged step, the recorded `DesiredStateId`, the workspace path, the `WIM_READY` flag, and the recorded source-content hash. The fifth field (source hash) was introduced on `WIM_READY` checkpoints in v47 patch 1 and extended to Step 3 checkpoints in v47 patch 2. Relevant for v47 checkpoint-invalidation bugs (`Checkpoint step N source identity ... does not match the currently-selected source`) and stale-workspace resume issues. -->
- **Partition deferral marker:** <!-- if C:\Recovery\OEM\winre_partition_deferred.json exists, include its diagnostic fields; otherwise say "not present". Redact sensitive paths. In v50 patch 5, Capacity deferrals are reassessed on the next run; Execution deferrals use a bounded one-hour retry delay. The marker's presence alone does not mean a repair was skipped. -->
- **Pending deployment (v50 patch 5):** <!-- if %ProgramData%\OEM\WinRE-Manager\pending-deployment.json exists, report its phase/disposition and the logged refusal or verification result. Preserve this record and its pending.wim; do not delete them to force a retry. Redact sensitive paths before sharing. -->
- **Resume task present (v49):** <!-- query: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'WinRE Manager - Resume' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue. If it exists, paste its State, LastRunTime, NextRunTime, and the action's Arguments (the "Task To Run" field from `schtasks /query /tn "WinRE Manager - Resume" /v /fo list`). If it does not exist, say so. -->
  <!-- Live Repair and Restore attempt to register a resume task; DryRun and early refusals do not. A task left after exit can indicate interruption, a pending operation or an unresolved failure. Include the task action and relevant log lines. The action normally runs the verified staged script at C:\Recovery\OEM\Resume\WinRE.ps1; a fileless invocation cannot stage it. A staging failure can skip registration with a warning, but an unsafe existing task that cannot be confirmed removed forces a fatal exit. Do not delete pending recovery material to force a retry. -->
- **Manager config file (v50):** <!-- if it exists, paste the contents of C:\ProgramData\OEM\WinRE-Manager\manager.json. Otherwise say "not present". -->
  <!-- The manager config file was introduced in v50 patch 1. It holds the backup-root catalogue read by the Cleanup-Backups.ps1 helper. Its containing directory, its immediate parent, and the config file itself must pass the shared trust check: owner is SYSTEM or Administrators, and no Allow ACE grants a modify-capable right to a principal outside SYSTEM, Administrators, or TrustedInstaller. The manager treats a config that fails the check as an untrusted config and falls back to the empty default (which is a silent behavior change, not a failure). If the backup action reported an inability to register the destination root, or the Cleanup helper did not find a backup you know exists, paste the file here along with the ACLs of `C:\ProgramData\OEM\WinRE-Manager`, `C:\ProgramData\OEM`, and the config file itself `manager.json` (from `Get-Acl -Path <dir> | Format-List Owner, AccessToString`). -->
- **Backup destination (if the failing action was Backup):** <!-- the destination path as entered, and the free space at that path from `Get-PSDrive -Name <letter>` or `Get-Volume -DriveLetter <letter>` -->
  <!-- The backup action runs a free-space preflight before creating the destination directory. It requires the source WIM size plus a 100 MiB margin. If the preflight failed, the log names the required and available byte counts. If the destination is a mapped network drive, the preflight falls back to Get-PSDrive. A destination whose free space cannot be determined proceeds without preflight; the failure is surfaced by Copy-Item. -->
- **Elevation:** <!-- Running as SYSTEM, as admin, unelevated -->
- **7-Zip present:** <!-- yes/no -->
- **Concurrent invocation:** <!-- was any other WinRE.ps1 process running at the same time? Scheduled task, manual invocation, RMM tool "run now", Intune remediation. -->
  <!-- If the run exited with code 2 and the log contains "Another WinRE Manager instance is already running (program lock file is exclusively held)", this is expected behavior, not a bug. The other instance is doing the work. -->
  <!-- If the run exited with code 3 and the log contains "Cannot rename because item at '<workspace>\winre.wim' does not exist" and an earlier line contains "Could not set up program lock at …", the lock could not be acquired for a non-contention reason and the run proceeded unprotected. Include the exact lock-failure message and the permissions on C:\ProgramData\OEM\Logs\. -->
  <!-- If the run exited with code 3 and the log contains "FATAL: WinRE Manager requires an elevated (Administrator) PowerShell session", this is expected behavior as of v48 patch 2, not a bug. The guard refuses unelevated launches in milliseconds rather than failing several minutes later at Mount-WindowsImage. The fix is to relaunch from an elevated prompt or via `scripts\WinRE-Manager.cmd`. -->

## Log

**If your log contains any of the following lines, please copy the surrounding context** (10–20 lines before and after). These are the exact signatures the maintainer wants to see for the corresponding failure mode:

- `Another WinRE Manager instance is already running` — concurrent-instance deferral. Not a failure; the other instance is doing the work.
- `Deferring WinRE Manager: Windows is not in a normal-running state` — Audit Mode / OOBE / sysprep deferral.
- `VMD hardware detection was indeterminate; deferring` — fail-closed VMD check. Include the enumeration error from the line above.
- `OS-fallback deferred: C: could not be confirmed fully decrypted` — OS-fallback route refused. Include C:'s `Test-VolumeEncrypted` value.
- `Dedicated replacement deferred before partition deletion (<Reason>)` — pre-shrink deferral. Include the exact `<Reason>` string, the free space on the resize target named in that reason, and the total size of that target.
- `Image injection did not complete. Stopping before Step 4` — Step 3 → Step 4 pipeline gate. Include the injection failure reason (OEM download, extraction, INF validation, or VMD driver download).
- `Enable-only /enable failed (attempt N of 3)` or `Enable-only /enable refused with the BitLocker error` — enable-failure counter. Include the state file's `LastEnableResult` and `EnableFailureAttempts`.
- `Offline fallback: the machine requires a full update` or `Offline fallback: using state file's stored DesiredStateId` — offline fallback. Include whether the machine was actually offline and the state file's `LastUpdated`.
- `Extension-failure fallback: creating recovery partition` or `Extension-failure fallback unavailable` — post-delete extension failure. Include the plan's bucket size, the trailing unallocated extent size, and the current C: end and disk end.
- `Pre-deletion inventory:` followed in the same run by `OS-fallback deferred: C: could not be confirmed fully decrypted` — the post-deletion residual corner. **Capture the full log and the machine's end state.** The project wants field data on this corner.
- `Refusing to retry reagentc /enable` — enable-failure loop-breaker. The state file still records the counter; the operator resolves the cause, deletes the state file, re-runs.
- `Planned recovery extent is no longer free after deletion (offset=... size=... overlapCount=0)` with an `alignment reserve` value in the plan summary — the v45 plan-rejection corner fixed by v46 patch 1. Include the top-of-log version banner and the `alignment reserve` value.
- `Strip stage failed - candidate rejected` — the v47 strip stage rejected the candidate. Include the specific strip failure reason from the preceding line (enumeration, removal, missing INF field, or budget exhaustion) and the pre-strip inventory lines.
- `Registered-source recheck at <site> : CHANGED` followed by `Registered WinRE source changed during candidate preparation` — the v47 race detector fired. Include the captured fingerprint line, the recheck line, the change triple (`location=<bool> version=<bool> hash=<bool>`), and whether a Windows Update was in flight.
- `State has no DeployedWinREMetadata anchor`, `Registered WinRE metadata changed from … to …`, or `Registered WinRE metadata could not be read` — the v47 metadata-based rebuild trigger fired. Include the state file's `DeployedWinREMetadata` value and the currently-registered WinRE's `Version` / `SPBuild`.
- `CmdletizationQuery_NotFound_DiskNumber` or `No MSFT_Partition objects found with property 'DiskNumber'` — the SD/MMC read. Note the disk number and whether the machine has a card reader or an empty USB enclosure attached.
- `Base WIM copy hash mismatch: source=..., copied=...` — the v47 patch 2 copy-integrity check rejected the candidate. Include the source path, the source hash, the copied hash, and the currently-registered WinRE metadata (in case the source changed during acquisition).
- `Base WIM copy is unreadable after Copy-Item` — the copy-integrity check could not read the destination. Include the source path and the source hash.
- `Could not confirm removal: <path>` — the v47 patch 3 `Remove-ItemIfExist` verification fired. Include the path, its parent directory contents, and whether a lock or ACL was suspected.
- `Checkpoint step N has no recorded source identity` — a legacy (v47 patch 1 Step 3) or GitHub-sourced checkpoint was invalidated on first resume. Include the checkpoint's recorded Step value.
- `Checkpoint step N source identity ... does not match the currently-selected source ...` — the recorded source identity no longer matches the current selection rules. Include the recorded hash, the currently-selected hash, and the source-selection `Reason` string.
- `Checkpoint step N source identity ... cannot be re-validated` — no source was available to validate the checkpoint against. Include the recorded hash.
- `Registered WinRE candidate is present at ... but its servicing metadata could not be read` — the source-selection helper could not read the registered WIM's DISM servicing metadata. Include the path.
- `A WIM was discovered at ... but not at the registered location` — the loose fallback-discovery path found a WIM outside the registered location. Include the path and whether the registered location yielded a readable WIM.
- `WinRE is registered via OS-fallback (location: ...) but its winre.wim could not be read at that location (status=...) - forcing rebuild` — the v47 patch 2 OS-fallback missing-WIM guard fired. Include the registered location, the `reagentc /info` status, and whether `C:\Recovery\WindowsRE\winre.wim` exists.
- `All three methods failed for <letter>: - <diagnostic>` — drive-letter assignment exhausted one of the 26 candidate letters. The `<diagnostic>` names the reason (for example `diskpart: The specified drive letter is not free to be assigned` for a letter reserved by a mapped network drive). Include the diagnostic string, the full `All three methods failed for ...` lines from the log, and the current drive letters reported by `Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem` and `net use`.
- `Invoke-DriveLetterAssignment: target partition <n>/<m> no longer exists` — the target partition was removed mid-search. Include what deleted it (a concurrent tool, an operator action, or a failed prior step) and the current partition inventory from `Get-Partition`.
- `Invoke-DriveLetterAssignment: target disk <n> is <offline|status>` — the disk holding the target partition went offline or is not Online. Include the disk state from `Get-Disk -Number <n> | Format-List` and whether the disk came back online after the run.
- `WinRE is Enabled but its registered location ... could not be resolved to a partition` or `WinRE is Enabled but reagentc reports no registered location` — the v48 patch 1 fail-closed pre-shrink guard. Include the `reagentc /info` output verbatim, the partition inventory from `Get-Partition`, and whether the registered location is a `GLOBALROOT\...` or `Volume{...}` path.
- `Intervening-anchor plan: anchor is disk <n> part <m>; anchor shrink <N> MiB` — the v48 intervening-anchor path entered. Include the anchor partition's current size, filesystem, type code, BitLocker state, and drive letter, plus the full partition inventory from `Get-Partition -DiskNumber <n>`.
- `anchor is ... ; refusing to shrink` or `anchor is BitLocker-locked` or `anchor encryption state is indeterminate` or `anchor has no drive letter` — the v48 anchor validation rejected. Include the specific rejection reason from the log and the anchor partition's properties.
- `intervening anchor is <N> MiB smaller than the plan requires` — the v48 surplus rejection. Include the anchor's current size, the required bucket size, and the size of the recovery partition being reclaimed.
- `recovery-typed partitions exist beyond the intervening anchor's recovery cluster` — the v48 multi-intervening rejection. Include the full partition layout from `Get-Partition -DiskNumber <n>`.
- `Unsupported OS architecture '<arch>'` — the v48 architecture gate refusal. Include `[Environment]::Is64BitOperatingSystem`, `$env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE`, `$env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITEW6432`, and the output of `Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object OSArchitecture, Caption, BuildNumber`.
- `Offline fallback: stored LocalInputsId <hash> does not match the current locally-computable inputs <hash>` — the v48 offline hardware-drift guard. Include both hashes and the state file's `LastUpdated`.
- `Preserving existing target ... as rollback copy` or `Deploy-WimTransactional ... copy failed - restoring rollback copy` or `Deploy-WimTransactional ... rollback restore hash verification failed` or `Rollback copy restored to <path>` — the v48 transactional WIM replacement. Include the source path, target path, source hash, target hash (if any), and whether the rollback restore hash-verified.
- `FATAL: WinRE Manager requires an elevated (Administrator) PowerShell session` — the v48 patch 2 fail-fast elevation guard. This is expected behavior, not a bug. The fix is to relaunch from an elevated prompt or via `scripts\WinRE-Manager.cmd`. The script exits with code 3 in this case.

**v49 log signatures.** The v49 features add the following log lines. Include them verbatim if your run failed in a way that mentions one of them:

- **Source-ownership classification.** `Source-ownership classification: <Class> - <Reason>` — the classification decision. `<Class>` is one of `Manager-Owned`, `Manager-Lineage`, `Foreign-No-Drivers`, `Foreign-With-Drivers`. Include the full line.
- **`Foreign-With-Drivers` preservation.** Patch 5 logs `Foreign source preserved byte-identically; assessing dedicated layout without strip, injection or export.` Include the classification and subsequent deployment/deferral lines: preservation can now include relocation to an adequate dedicated partition. Older versions reported preservation with no deployment.
- **Never-downgrade check.** `Never-downgrade invariant: candidate image would replace an existing storage driver with an older version. Preserving the source; no deployment.` followed by one `  Downgrade: <inf> : source <ver> -> candidate <ver>` line per detected downgrade. Include all the `Downgrade:` lines.
- **Storage applicability gate (input).** `Storage applicability: parsed <n> INF(s) and collected <m> unique hardware ID(s); machine has <k> SCSIAdapter-class device(s)`. Followed by one `Storage applicability: controller '<name>' has a matching INF in the candidate image` line per matched controller, and — on refusal — one `Storage applicability: controller '<name>' (InstanceId <id>) has NO matching INF in the candidate image - hardware IDs considered: <ids>` line per unmatched controller.
- **Storage applicability gate (verdict).** `Storage applicability: Applicable=True, Controllers=<k>, Matched=<k>, Reason=all <k> storage controller(s) have at least one matching INF` on success; `Storage applicability gate rejected the candidate: <Reason>. Dismounting with -Discard and deferring.` on refusal. **The refusal has never fired in the field — a field log of it is high-signal.** Include the full `Storage applicability:` block above the refusal line, the manifest version, and the candidate's injection source (OEM pack resolution, VMD package resolution, or both).
- **Native-boot VHDX fail-closed gate.** `Native-boot VHDX gate refused: <Reason>` — the OS volume is on a native-boot VHDX with a physical host disk visible. Include the full line, plus the output of `Get-Disk | Format-List Number, FriendlyName, BusType, Location` and `Get-Volume`.
- **Backup action (success path).** `Backup destination: <path>`, `Backup source WIM: <path>`, `Backup source WIM size: <n> MiB, SHA256: <hash>`, `Backup copy hash verified: <hash>`, `Wrote backup sidecar: <path>`.
- **Backup action (failure paths).** `Backup cannot proceed: <reason>` for a refusal; `Backup copy failed: <error>` for a copy failure; `Backup copy hash verification failed (source=<hash>, dest=<hash>).` for a hash mismatch; `Backup sidecar write failed: <error> - the WIM is present and verified; sidecar is metadata only` for a sidecar-only failure (exit code 2). Include the full failure line and the `Backup source WIM:` line above it.
- **Restore action (success path).** `Restore target: <path> (mode=DEDICATED|OS-FALLBACK)`, followed by `Restore: target WIM replaced and hash-verified`, `reagentc /setreimage: exit=<n>, output=...`, and `reagentc /enable result: <ok|reboot|failed|bitlocker>`.
- **Restore action (mid-transformation failures).** `Restore failed at reagentc /setreimage: <output>` (exit code 3; the state file, checkpoint, and deferral marker are deleted, and the resume task is preserved) and `Restore: WIM replaced but reagentc /enable returned <failed|bitlocker>. The WIM is in place; a subsequent repair run or manual reagentc /enable may resolve.` (exit code 2; resume task preserved). **Neither path has been exercised in the field — a field log of either is high-signal.**
- **Restore action (refusals and aborts).** `Restore cannot proceed: <reason>` for a pre-flight refusal — the reason names the specific failure (backup directory missing, no `winre.wim` in the backup, backup WIM unreadable, no registered WinRE route, target route is not a recognized type, no drive letter available, registered location did not resolve, OS-fallback target not fully decrypted, target recovery partition not ready, WinRE status indeterminate). `Restore aborted: reagentc /disable failed (exit <n>). The existing WinRE route is intact; no changes were made.` and `Restore aborted: WinRE still reports <status> after reagentc /disable.` for the disable-step failures. `Restore failed: the target WIM replacement did not complete. Attempting to re-enable WinRE.` for the transactional-replacement failure. Include the full line and the `Restore target:` line above it.
- **Temporary resume task.** `Registered temporary resume task 'WinRE Manager - Resume' (boot +1m, one-shot T+1h); it will be removed on clean completion` at registration. `Found an existing 'WinRE Manager - Resume' task; re-registering with -Force (this is expected when the resume task re-registers itself, and is the recovery path when a previous run was interrupted)` when a previous task was already present. `Removed temporary resume task 'WinRE Manager - Resume'` at clean completion. `Could not register the temporary resume task 'WinRE Manager - Resume': <error> - the repair pipeline will proceed without self-healing` when registration failed. `Could not register the Ctrl+C handler for the resume task: <error> - Ctrl+C will proceed through the normal cleanup path and the task will be removed` when the compiled Ctrl+C delegate could not be registered. `Register-ResumeTask: script was not invoked from a file (`$PSCommandPath is not populated; this is the gist-bootstrap or paste-into-console case). Skipping the temporary resume task - the repair pipeline itself is unaffected.` under gist-bootstrap or paste-into-console invocation.
- **Wrapper stable install location.** Emitted by `WinRE-Manager.cmd`, not by `WinRE.ps1`; the output goes to the elevated child window, not to `WinRE-Manager.log`. Success path: `Automatic WinRE maintenance installed.` followed by `Task: <name>`, `Run as: NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`, `Script: <dst>`, and `SHA256: <dstHash>`. Patch 5 also checks destination trust, staging and final verification. On failure, include the complete `Automatic maintenance installation failed:` output and the relevant paths/hashes after redaction.

**v50 patch 1 log signatures.** The v50 features add the following log lines. Include them verbatim if your run failed in a way that mentions one of them:

**Successor note (v50 patch 3).** Five of the signatures below were superseded in v50 patch 3. The two manager-config ownership-gate signatures were replaced by the extended trust-gate wording. The three resume-task protected-path guard signatures were replaced by the resume-script staging design. Both descriptions below are accurate as of v50 patch 1. See the v50 patch 3 log signatures section further down for the current signatures.

- **Ownership migration hash bridge.** `Ownership migration bridge: using historical CurrentImageHash from stale state file (<hash>) so the last-known-good copy is recognized across a version boundary` and `Ownership migration bridge: using historical LineageId from stale state file (<id>) so the source-ownership classifier can validate a marker across a version boundary`. These fire on the first v50 run on a machine whose state file was written by v49 or earlier. Include the state file's `CurrentImageHash`, `LineageId`, and `LastUpdated`, plus the source-ownership classification line that follows.
- **Source-ownership classification with historical bridge.** `Source-ownership classification: Manager-Owned - staged source hash matches historical CurrentImageHash (<hash>)`. This is the expected outcome when the migration bridge fired and the classifier recognized the source as manager-owned. If instead you see `Foreign-With-Drivers` on a machine that ran under v49, the bridge did not fire — include the state file's `CurrentImageHash` and the source's actual SHA256.
- **Resume-task protected-path guard refusal.** `Register-ResumeTask: '<scriptDir>' grants write-capable access to '<principal>' (FileSystemRights=<rights>). Registering the resume task against a script in a non-admin-writable location would allow a non-administrator to modify the file and have it execute as SYSTEM on the next boot. Skipping the temporary resume task; the repair pipeline itself is unaffected.` Include the log line and the ACL of the script directory from `Get-Acl -Path '<scriptDir>' | Format-List Owner, AccessToString`. If the script was launched from a OneDrive-synced folder, say so — the guard was specifically designed so that OneDrive paths are correctly evaluated (the `Test-Path -PathType Container` check the previous code used returned `$false` there).
- **Resume-task ACL unreadable.** `Register-ResumeTask: could not read the ACL of '<scriptDir>': <error> - skipping the temporary resume task (fail closed; the repair pipeline itself is unaffected)`. Include the error text and whether the script directory is on a network path or a reparse point.
- **Resume-task script directory unreadable.** `Register-ResumeTask: could not determine the directory containing '<PSCommandPath>' - skipping the temporary resume task (the repair pipeline itself is unaffected)`. Very rare; include the log line.
- **Backup free-space preflight refusal.** `Backup cannot proceed: destination <destRoot> has insufficient free space (<n> MiB free, need <n> MiB). No backup was written.` Include both byte counts, the `Backup free-space check:` line above it (which names the destination free space source — `Get-Volume` or `Get-PSDrive`), and the destination path as entered.
- **Backup destination drive letter does not resolve.** `Backup cannot proceed: destination drive letter <letter> in <path> does not resolve to a known local or mapped drive.` Include the path as entered, the output of `Get-PSDrive -Name <letter>`, and whether the drive is a mapped network drive.
- **Backup UNC resolution.** `Add-ManagerBackupRoot: resolved mapped drive <letter>: to UNC path <unc> for catalogue storage`. This is an informational line, not a failure — include it if the backup's destination was entered as a mapped-drive path and the subsequent cleanup helper cannot find the backup.
- **Manager config ownership gate refusal (read path).** `Get-ManagerConfig: ancestor directory '<path>' is not owned by SYSTEM or Administrators - treating config as empty`. Include the ACL of both the containing directory and its immediate parent from `Get-Acl`. This is the expected outcome when someone other than SYSTEM or Administrators owns `C:\ProgramData\OEM\WinRE-Manager` or `C:\ProgramData\OEM`.
- **Manager config ownership gate refusal (write path).** `Refusing to write manager config: ancestor directory '<path>' is not owned by SYSTEM or Administrators. The config remains the empty default.` Same ACL information as above. This is a refusal, not a crash — a subsequent backup still completes; only the catalogue entry is skipped.
- **Manager config ancestor could not be checked.** `Test-PathTrustedForSystem: could not read ACL of '<path>' : <error> - fail closed` and `Test-PathTrustedForSystem: could not determine owner of '<path>' - fail closed`. Both are fail-closed paths. Include the exact error text and the ACL form of the directory.
- **Empty workspace parent removal refused.** `Could not remove empty workspace parent '<parent>' - a process may hold a handle to it; leaving it in place`. Informational; not a failure. Include the parent path and whether a process (Explorer, VS Code, or the invoking PowerShell session's working directory) may be holding the folder.
- **Empty test parent removal refused (harness).** `Could not remove empty test parent '<parent>' - a process may hold a handle to it; leaving it in place` — the same message pattern emitted by Test-WinRE.ps1. If the harness cleanup left `C:\Temp` behind, this line tells you why.
- **Stray-recovery cleanup aggregate summary (v50; extended v50 patch 2).** `Stray-recovery cleanup summary: deleted: <list>; preserved oversized: <list>; preserved virtual: <list>; skipped non-typed: <list>` in live mode, or `Stray-recovery cleanup summary (DRY RUN): would delete: <list>; preserved oversized: <list>; preserved virtual: <list>; skipped non-typed: <list>` in DryRun. This line is emitted on every run and enumerates what was (or would be) deleted, preserved-oversized, preserved-virtual (mounted VHD/VHDX disks, v50 patch 2), skipped-non-typed, or failed. If a stray recovery partition you expected to be preserved was deleted, or one you expected to be deleted was preserved, this summary is the line to quote.

**v50 patch 2 log signatures.** The v50 patch 2 features add the following log lines. Include them verbatim if your run failed in a way that mentions one of them:

- **Non-OS sweep suppression (hypervisor detected).** `Stray-recovery cleanup: skipping the non-OS-disk sweep because a known hypervisor signature was detected. Any recovery partitions on non-OS disks are preserved. The OS-disk repair path is unaffected.` — the running OS was detected inside a known hypervisor and the entire non-OS-disk sweep was suppressed. Include this line, the `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine: signature '<sig>' matched ...` line above it, and the output of `Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem | Select-Object Manufacturer, Model`.
- **Non-OS sweep suppression (indeterminate).** `Stray-recovery cleanup: skipping the non-OS-disk sweep because detection was indeterminate (fail closed). Any recovery partitions on non-OS disks are preserved. The OS-disk repair path is unaffected.` — the hypervisor detection could not produce a verdict, so the sweep was suppressed as the safe direction. Include this line and the `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine:` diagnostic above it (`could not read Win32_ComputerSystem: <error>`, `Win32_ComputerSystem returned nothing`, or `Manufacturer and Model are both unavailable - treating as indeterminate (fail closed)`).
- **Hypervisor-detection verdict lines.** `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine: signature '<sig>' matched (Manufacturer='<mfg>', Model='<mdl>') -> guest environment`, `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine: no known hypervisor signature (Manufacturer='<mfg>', Model='<mdl>') -> treating as physical`, `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine: Manufacturer and Model are both unavailable - treating as indeterminate (fail closed)`, `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine: could not read Win32_ComputerSystem: <error> - treating as indeterminate (fail closed)`, and `Test-RunningInVirtualMachine: Win32_ComputerSystem returned nothing - treating as indeterminate (fail closed)`. One of these is emitted on every run. Include it if the machine is a VM and the sweep's behavior is unexpected.
- **File Backed Virtual disk preservation.** `Stray-recovery cleanup: preserving File Backed Virtual (mounted VHD/VHDX) disk <n> - a mounted virtual disk may contain another installation's recovery environment` — the sweep skipped a mounted VHD/VHDX. Include this line and the disk's `BusType` from `Get-Disk -Number <n> | Format-List BusType, FriendlyName`.

**v50 patch 3 log signatures.** The v50 patch 3 release renames the two manager-config trust-check messages, replaces the v50 patch 1 resume-task protected-path guard with the resume-script staging design, and adds several new signatures. Include them verbatim if your run failed in a way that mentions one of them:

- **Manager config trust gate refusal (read path).** `Get-ManagerConfig: ancestor directory '<path>' is not trusted (owner is not SYSTEM or Administrators, or a non-admin principal holds write-capable permissions) - treating config as empty` and the new file-level variant `Get-ManagerConfig: config file '<path>' is not trusted (owner is not SYSTEM or Administrators, or a non-admin principal holds write-capable permissions on it) - treating config as empty`. The v50 patch 1 wording ("is not owned by SYSTEM or Administrators") is superseded; a machine running v50 patch 3 emits the new wording.
- **Manager config trust gate refusal (write path).** `Refusing to write manager config: ancestor directory '<path>' is not trusted (owner is not SYSTEM or Administrators, or a non-admin principal holds write-capable permissions). The config remains the empty default.` and `Refusing to write manager config: existing config file '<path>' is not trusted (owner is not SYSTEM or Administrators, or a non-admin principal holds write-capable permissions on it). The config remains unchanged.` Same reasoning.
- **Resume-script staging messages.** `Resume-script staging: staged <src> -> <dst> (SHA256=<hash>)` on successful staging (this is the normal case). `Resume-script staging: running from the staged copy (<path>); reusing it` when the resume task itself fires and re-invokes the script from the staged path (self-staging short-circuit). `Register-ResumeTask: could not stage the running script to a trusted location. Skipping the temporary resume task; the repair pipeline itself is unaffected.` when staging fails at any step (staging-directory creation, script copy, hash verification, or the final trust check) — the pipeline proceeds without the resume hook. `Resume-script staging: hash mismatch after copy (source=<src>, staged=<dst>)`, `Resume-script staging: staged file <path> is not trusted after staging`, `Resume-script staging: staging directory <path> is not trusted after staging`, and `Resume-script staging: could not create <path> with a strict DACL: <error>` when a specific staging step failed. Include the exact warning line and the ACLs of the staging directory and its ancestors.
- **Trust-helper detailed refusals.** `Test-PathTrustedForSystem: '<path>' is owned by SID <sid>, which is neither SYSTEM nor Administrators - refusing` for an untrusted owner, and `Test-PathTrustedForSystem: '<path>' grants write-capable access to '<principal>' (SID=<sid>, FileSystemRights=<rights>) - refusing` for a permissive ACE. The latter names the specific principal and rights that tripped the mask.
- **Stray-recovery sweep post-deletion verification failure.** `Stray-recovery cleanup: post-deletion verification query failed for <ref> : <error> - treating as not-confirmed-deleted (fail closed)` when the re-query itself threw, and `Stray-recovery cleanup: stray recovery partition <ref> still present after Remove-Partition returned success` when the partition survived the delete. Either means the sweep did not confirm the removal.
- **GitHub empty archive-parts guard.** `Get-GitHubBaseWinRE: no winre.7z.NNN archive parts found at <url>` — the folder was reachable but its contents no longer match the expected filename pattern.
- **Restore resume-task persist on deployment failure.** `Restore deployment failure: WinRE could not be confirmed Enabled after the re-enable attempt (result=<result>) - preserving the temporary resume task so the operation is resumed on the next boot or within the hour` — the WIM-replacement step failed and the follow-up re-enable did not return `ok`.
- **Cleanup-Backups.ps1 reparse-point skip.** `  Skipping reparse point: <path>` during discovery; `  Skipping reparse point (refusing to recurse): <name>` during deletion; and `  Skipping unreadable candidate: <path>` when the discovery-time `Get-Item` threw. None is a failure of the helper; each is the file's policy not to recurse through a junction or symlink.
- **Cleanup-Backups.ps1 WIM-ONLY tag.** The listing shows a `[WIM-ONLY, no sidecar]` suffix on backups whose `backup.json` is missing or unparseable. These are listed and deletable; the production restore action handles them with reduced verification.
- **Fail-closed drive-letter normalization.** `Could not verify whether <letter>: contains \Windows (<error>) - skipping drive-letter removal for this recovery volume (fail closed)` — the provider error on the `\Windows` presence check skipped letter removal for one recovery volume rather than aborting the whole run.
- **Fail-closed workspace volume enumeration.** `Get-WorkDirCandidates: could not enumerate volumes: <error> - no workspace candidates will be offered (fail closed; caller will defer)` — a Storage-module error during volume enumeration deferred the full-update path cleanly instead of aborting FATAL.
- **ACE-catch fail-closed correction in `Test-PathTrustedForSystem`.** `Test-PathTrustedForSystem: could not resolve the SID for an ACE on '<path>' (IdentityReference='<principal>') - fail closed` - the ACE loop now logs and returns `$false` on an unresolvable SID rather than silently skipping the ACE, honouring the header comment's fail-closed contract. The same correction was ported to the duplicated trust helper in `Cleanup-Backups.ps1` (which writes through `Write-Host`, so the message does not appear in the log file) and to the compressed inline trust check in `WinRE-Manager.cmd`'s Restore `TARGET_COMMAND` (which uses `return $false` without a log line). The production branch is rarely reached in practice.
- **Restore-failure state invalidation.** On the WIM-deployment-failure path, the branch now compares the target WIM's SHA256 from before the deploy attempt against its value after the failure. `Restore failure: target WIM is unchanged from the pre-restore state (SHA256=<hash>); preserving state file, checkpoint, and deferral marker` - the target is provably unchanged (untouched, or the transactional rollback restored and hash-verified it), so the three markers are preserved. `Restore failure: target WIM cannot be proven unchanged (before=<hash>, after=<hash>); invalidating state file, checkpoint, and deferral marker so the next run does not trust stale state` - the target differs or one hash is unavailable (`Get-LiveWimHash` returns `$null` for both absent and unreadable); the three markers are invalidated and the resume-task persist flag is set unconditionally in the invalidate branch. The `before` field reads `(unavailable before restore, or absent)` and the `after` field reads `(unavailable after failure)` when the corresponding hash could not be captured. The opening line on this path was reworded to `Restore failed: the target WIM replacement did not complete. Attempting to re-enable WinRE.`

---

**Why we ask for all this.** The script's design is organized around four invariants — *never break Windows RE*, *never leave a machine without a working recovery route*, *minimize the `reagentc /disable` → `reagentc /enable` window*, and *do no work unless needed; prepare everything before touching anything*. See [`docs/architecture.md`](https://github.com/ArthurJDurand/WinRE-Manager/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) for the full hierarchy. The fields above are the ones that let the maintainer determine which invariant was involved in your failure and reproduce it. [`docs/deployment.md`](https://github.com/ArthurJDurand/WinRE-Manager/blob/main/docs/deployment.md) translates the invariants into deployment-time guidance, [`docs/troubleshooting.md`](https://github.com/ArthurJDurand/WinRE-Manager/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md) maps log signatures to symptoms, and [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/ArthurJDurand/WinRE-Manager/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) documents the report requirements.
